Surah Ash-Shura

It is named "Ash-Shura" (the Consultation) because its verses indicate the lowliness of this world and the honour of the Hereafter, and the qualities of those who seek them, along with the unity of their hearts in every state. This is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an. So said al-Mahayimi. It is Meccan, though it is said that it contains a Medinan part. The verification of this has passed many times, and its number of verses is fifty-three.

The explanation of His words, exalted is He:

[3] ﴿Thus He reveals to you and to those before you, God, the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾

﴿Thus He reveals to you and to those before you, God, the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ This is a resumed statement (*kalam mustaʾnaf*, a sentence that begins a new thought and is not grammatically dependent on what precedes it). The verified view is that the content of the surah agrees with what is found within the other books revealed to the earlier messengers, in calling to monotheism (*tawhid*) and guiding to the truth. Or, its revelation is like its revelation: after glorifying it by mentioning its name and drawing attention to the greatness of its status. The *kaf* (the "thus") is in the accusative position, as an object of *yuhi* ("He reveals") according to the first view, and as an attribute (*naʿt*) of an emphatic infinitive (*maṣdar*) of it according to the second view. The *dhalika* ("that") refers, on the first view, to what is in the surah, and on the second, to its revelation. The sense of distance in it indicates the exalted rank of what is referred to and the distance of its station in excellence. That is: like the meanings in this surah, He revealed in the other surahs to you, and to those before you among the messengers in their books. Moreover, the basis of the likeness is what has been pointed to, namely the call to monotheism and the guidance to the truth, and what contains the welfare of the servants in this world and the next. Or, like its revelation: He revealed to you at the revelation of the other surahs, and to the other messengers at the revelation of their books to them, with no revelation different from it. This is as in His words: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah﴾ (an-Nisa 4:163), the verse... Moreover, the basis of the likeness is that it is conveyed through the angel. The use of the present tense (*mudariʿ*) is to narrate a past situation, indicating the continuity of revelation and that a revelation like it is His custom. In making the content of the surah, or its revelation, the thing compared (*mushabbah bihi*), there is a glorification of it that is not hidden. Likewise in describing Him with the two attributes of might and wisdom. The placement of the agent (*fawiʿl*) later is to observe the rhyme-endings (*fawasil*, the final sounds of verses), along with what it contains of arousing curiosity.

It is also read *yuhā* ("is revealed") in the passive voice, on the basis that *kadhalika* is the subject (*mubtadaʾ*) and *yuhi* is its predicate (*khabar*) attributed to its pronoun; or its verbal noun (*maṣdar*), and *yuhi* is attributed to *ilayka* ("to you"). And *Allah* is in the nominative case by what *yuhi* indicates, as if it were said: "Who reveals?" and it was answered: "Allah."

﴿the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ are two attributes of Him, or a subject (*mubtadaʾ*), as in the reading *nūḥī* ("We reveal"), and "the Almighty" and what follows it are two predicates of it; or "the Almighty, the All-Wise" are two attributes of Him. And His words, exalted is He:

The Interpretation of His Words, may He be exalted:

[4] ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great.﴾

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great.﴾ The two predicates are "خبران" (khabarān, two predicates) of "لَهُ" (lahu, "to Him"). According to the aforementioned readings, it is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) confirming His might and wisdom. This was conveyed by Abu al-Su'ud.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[5, 6] ﴿The heavens are almost rent asunder from above them, and the angels glorify their Lord with praise and seek forgiveness for those on earth. Verily, Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾ ﴿And those who take protectors besides Him, Allah is Watchful over them, and you are not a guardian over them.﴾ [al-Shura: 6]

(p-5222) ﴿The heavens are almost rent asunder from above them﴾ That is: they split apart, being affected by the manifestations of His greatness, and they would vanish from the height of His overpowering dominion and authority. This is indicated by what follows it: ﴿the Exalted, the Mighty﴾ [al-Shura: 4]. Or (it is) from their attributing to Him a son, as in Surat Maryam. ﴿And the angels glorify their Lord with praise and seek forgiveness for those on earth﴾ That is: they ask forgiveness for the sins of those on earth among the believers in Him. ﴿Verily, Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[7] ﴿And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it, and warn of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt: a party will be in the Garden and a party in the Blaze.﴾

﴿And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an that you may warn the Mother of Cities﴾, i.e., its people, and it is Makkah. ﴿And those around it﴾, i.e., from among the Arabs and all other people. ﴿And warn of the Day of Assembly﴾, i.e., the Day of Resurrection, on which the disgrace will be greatest, because creation will be gathered on it. ﴿About which there is no doubt: a party will be in the Garden and a party in the Blaze﴾, i.e., among them there will be a party in the Garden, and they are those who believed in God and followed what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) brought them. And a party in the Blaze, i.e., the kindled Fire, blazing upon its people, and they are those who disbelieved in God and opposed what His Messenger brought them.

The Interpretation of His Saying, Exalted is He:

[8] ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have made them one community, but He admits whom He wills into His mercy. And the wrongdoers—for them there is no protector or helper.﴾

(p-5223) ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have made them one community﴾, that is, people of one religion and one creed. ﴿But He admits whom He wills into His mercy﴾, that is, but He did not do so, so as to make them one community, because that would contradict what the wisdom of creating human beings requires, namely the diversity of their individuals, which entails the difference of their inclinations and their paths. For this reason He willed what their creation and their predisposition require. So He imposed obligations upon them and based their affair on what they choose. Thus He admits into His mercy whom He wills, and they are the believers, and into His punishment, the disbelievers.

Abu al-Su'ud said: There is no doubt that His willing, Exalted is He, for each of the two admissions is consequent upon the deserving of each of the two groups for entering its place. ﴿And the wrongdoers—for them there is no protector or helper﴾, that is, the disbelievers in Allah have no protector who will befriend them on the Day of Resurrection, nor a helper who will defend them against the punishment of Allah and rescue them from His chastisement, because He will admit them into His subjugation. The describing of them as wrongdoers is an indication of the justice of the believers in matters of belief, morals, deeds and actions, and that He, Exalted is He, befriends them and helps them.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[9, 10] ﴿Or have they taken protectors besides Him? But God is the Protector, and He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.﴾ ﴿Whatever you differ about, its judgment is with God. That is God, my Lord; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back.﴾ [al-Shura: 10].

﴿Or have they taken protectors besides Him?﴾ That is, they take them as protectors, although in reality they have no guardianship, since they have no power and no might. ﴿But God is the Protector﴾: He is the One who must be taken as protector alone, and it must be believed that He is the Master and the Lord without any other, because of His exalted guardianship over every thing, and His sovereignty and His judgment. The fa' (the "then" particle) is the answer to an implied condition, as if it were said, after the denial of every protector other than Him: If they mean a protector in truth, then God is the Protector in truth, and there is no protector besides Him. ﴿And He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent﴾: that is, He is the Giver of life, the Able, so how could the guardianship of anyone else be valid? (p-5224) His saying ﴿Whatever you differ about, its judgment is with God. That is God, my Lord; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back﴾ [al-Shura: 10] is a preparation for what comes after it, concerning the command to establish the religion and not to divide in it, which is God's injunction to His prophets and His law for His creation. It is also an indication that the disagreement of those who oppose, among the polytheists and disbelievers, ultimately returns to God Exalted, to His judgment and His decree, that there is no religion but His religion, no worship but His worship, no lawful thing but what He has made lawful, and no unlawful thing but what He has made unlawful. The aim is a refutation of the polytheists of Mecca and their likes, in their legislating what God did not permit, and their making the following of forefathers and the varieties of desires their judge. The surah is Meccan, yet the verse indicates that whatever those who differ disagree about and dispute over in any matter of contention must be referred for judgment to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and that no other's judgment should be preferred over his judgment. Compare His saying: ﴿If you dispute about anything, refer it to God and the Messenger﴾ [al-Nisa': 59]. It also indicates the return to the muhkam (the clear, unambiguous verses) of the Book of God and the apparent meaning of the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), when they differ over the interpretation (ta'wil) of a verse and it becomes unclear to them. And it indicates the committing to God Exalted of what the intellects cannot reach, by saying: "God knows best," as in His saying: ﴿They ask you about the spirit. Say: the spirit is of the command of my Lord﴾ [al-Isra': 85].

His saying ﴿That is God, my Lord﴾ [al-Shura: 10] is either with an implied "Say" (qul) before it, or it is a quotation of His saying (ﷺ). That is, the One whose attributes are these attributes is my Lord, not your gods whom you call upon besides Him, which are unable to do anything.

**The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[11] ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you mates from among yourselves, and of the cattle, mates. He multiplies you thereby. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾

﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you mates from among yourselves﴾, i.e., from their own kind, ﴿mates﴾, i.e., wives. ﴿And of the cattle, mates﴾, i.e., kinds of various sorts, or males and females. ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾, i.e., He increases you, from (*al-dharʾ*, "dispersal"), which is scattering. It is said: God *dhara'a* the creation, meaning He scattered them and multiplied them. It has also been explained as (He creates you). The pronoun in ﴿thereby﴾ refers to the womb or the wombs. Al-Zamakhshari said: i.e., in this arrangement, which is that He made mates for humans and cattle, so that between their males and females there is procreation and propagation. The pronoun in (*yadhrauukum*, "He multiplies you") refers to the addressees and the cattle, with the addressees who reason given precedence over what does not reason, in a mixed reference. If you say: what is the meaning of "He multiplies you in this arrangement"? Why was it not said "He multiplies you by it"? I say: He made this arrangement like a source and a mine for dispersal and multiplication. End of quotation.

It has been said that (*fī*, "in") is used figuratively to mean causation.

﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: In this there are two possibilities. One of them is that its meaning is: "There is nothing like Him," and the particle *kāf* ("like") is the one inserted into the sentence.

A third possibility remains, which is that *mithl* ("like") here means "attribute," i.e., there is no attribute like His attribute. A fourth, which is what the verifiers (*al-muḥaqqiqūn*) have relied upon, is that what is intended by "like Him" is His very essence, as in their saying: "One like you does not stint," with the aim of emphasizing its negation from him. For when it is negated from one who is similar to him, its negation from him is more fitting. Then this method was employed concerning One who has no like, glorified is He. The point of the emphasis is that the metonymy (*kināya*, a figure in which the meaning is expressed indirectly) is of the type of asserting a thing by means of evidence. The metonymy in the verse has been clarified in another way, which al-Shumunni pointed to: that it is a negation of the thing by negating its necessary concomitant, because the negation of the concomitant entails the negation of what it accompanies, as one says: "My brother Zayd has no brother." The brother of Zayd is the thing that is necessitated, and "brother" is its concomitant, since Zayd's brother must have a brother, who is Zayd. So this concomitant is negated, while the intended meaning is the negation of what it necessitates, i.e., Zayd has no brother, for if he had a brother, that brother would have a brother, who is Zayd. Likewise, the negation that the like of God has a like, and the intended meaning is the negation of His like, exalted is He. For if He had a like, He would be a like of that like, since likeness is established from both sides.

(p-5226) Therefore it is not valid to negate "his like" (i.e., the negation of the like of that like). In summary, the negation of the like of the like was stated absolutely, while its concomitant from the negation of the like was intended. One of the eminent scholars said: "I have long found something within myself about this. The gist of it is that the negation of the like is a necessary concomitant of the reality of the verse, whereas it has already been established that the verse implies its affirmation. That is why they interpreted it by the aforementioned possibilities. How, then, can it be understood that the affirmation and the negation of a thing are both necessary for one and the same thing, given their explicit statement that the incompatibility of concomitants entails the incompatibility of what they necessitate? And even if we grant that each of them is a concomitant of it, to restrict it to this and not that is arbitrary, while the aim is to invalidate its indication of the impossible, which cannot be achieved by our saying that it is not intended, as is not hidden. Then it became clear that the affirmation of a like is not definitively a necessary concomitant of the reality of the verse, but is merely possible, just as its negation is possible, although the first is closer. However, in the specific matter of this root, there is a counter-argument: that if He had a like, etc. Thus that possibility is nullified from its origin. Therefore, the reliance for the negation of a like rests on this definitive premise, unlike the example. Understand this."

Al-Isam said: This, i.e., the verse being a case of metonymy, is an opinion that the eminent scholars (*al-fuḥūl*) have accepted, and they preferred it on the grounds that metonymy is more eloquent than explicit statement, and that avoiding excess is more deserving of preference. In it there is a point of inquiry: the negation of the like of the like does not entail the negation of the like, because a thing is not the like of its like. Rather, the like is one that shares with a thing in an attribute, while the thing is stronger in it and in the position of the original, and the like is in the position that is attached to it and approximates it. End of quotation.

Al-Sialkuti refuted him, saying: What has been said, that the negation of the like of the like does not entail the negation of the like, because the like of a thing is weaker than it, is pure delusion, for likeness is sharing in the most specific attributes, and equality in all aspects is what makes for likeness. This was stated in the *Sharḥ al-ʿAqāʾid al-Nasafiyya*. End.

Such literary subtleties are among the things that adorn the necks of understandings, and among whose valleys of marvels the springs of the beauties of speech flow.

**Note:**

Al-Suyuti said in *al-Iklil*: In the verse there is a refutation of the *Mushabbiha* (anthropomorphists), and that He, exalted is He, is neither a substance nor a body, nor an accident nor a colour, nor does He dwell in a place or a time. End.

(p-5227) It would have been proper to complete the deduction: just as the opening of the verse contains a refutation of the *Mushabbiha*, so too its conclusion, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾, is a refutation of the *Muʿaṭṭila* (those who deny God's attributes). That is why the most just of the schools of thought is the school of the *Salaf* (the early pious generations), for they affirmed the texts together with transcendence, without negation (*taʿṭīl*) and without likening (*tashbīh*). This is because the negators did not understand from the names and attributes of God, exalted is He, anything other than what is fitting for the created. Then they set about negating those understood meanings, so they combined likening and negation: they likened first and negated afterwards. Thus this is a likening and comparing on their part, of the concept of His names and attributes to the concept of the names and attributes of His creation, and then they negated what is due to Him, glorified and exalted is He, of the names and attributes befitting Him, may He be glorified and exalted. In contrast, the *Salaf* of this community and its distinguished imams describe God, glorified and exalted is He, with what He described Himself with, and with what He described His Prophet ﷺ with, without distortion (*taḥrīf*) and without likening. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾. Thus He refuted the *Mushabbiha* by negating likeness, and refuted the *Muʿaṭṭila* by His saying: ﴿and He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾.

The Hafiz Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: The People of the Sunna (*Ahl al-Sunna*) are unanimous in affirming the attributes mentioned in the Book and the Sunna, and in taking them in their literal sense, not in a figurative sense, except that they did not specify the modality (*takyīf*) of any of them. As for the *Jahmiyya*, the *Muʿtazila*, and the *Khawarij*, all of them deny these attributes and take none of them in their literal sense, and they claim that whoever affirms them is an anthropomorphist. Yet in the view of those who affirm them, they are the ones who negate the Worshipped One. End.

Al-Dhahabi said: He spoke the truth, by God! For whoever interprets all the attributes and takes what is related of them in a figurative sense of speech, that negation leads him to the nullification (*taʿṭīl*) of the Lord and to resemble the non-existent. This is as is related from Hammad ibn Zayd, who said: The likeness of the *Jahmiyya* is like a people who said: "In our house there is a palm tree." It was said to them: "Does it have fronds?" They said: "No." It was said: "Does it have a trunk?" They said: "No." It was said: "Does it have dates?" They said: "No." It was said: "Does it have a trunk?" They said: "No." It was said: "Then there is no palm tree in your house." I say: Likewise these negators, who say: "Our god is God, exalted is He, and He is not in a time, nor in a place, and He does not see, nor hear, nor perceive, nor speak, nor is He pleased, nor does He will, nor [such and such], nor [such and such]," and they say: "Glory be to the One transcendent above attributes!" Rather, we say: Glory be to God, the Exalted, the Mighty, the Hearing, the Seeing, the Willing, who spoke to Moses with direct speech, who took Abraham as a friend, who will be seen in the Hereafter, who is described by what He described Himself with, and by what His messengers described Him with, (p-5228) transcendent above the marks of created things and above the denial of those who deny Him. ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾

Al-Dhahabi, may God have mercy on him, also said: The position of the later theologians (*mutakallimūn*) is that God, exalted is He, is not in heaven, nor upon the Throne, nor upon the heavens, nor on the earth, nor inside the world, nor outside the world, nor is He separate from His creation, nor joined to them. They said: All these things are attributes of bodies, and God, exalted is He, is transcendent above body. The People of the Sunna and of the Narrations said to them: We do not delve into this, and we say what we have mentioned, following the texts, and we do not say according to your saying. For these negations are descriptions of the non-existent. Exalted is God, majestic in His majesty, above non-existence. Rather, He is existent, distinct from His creation, described by what He described Himself with, that He is above the Throne without modality. End.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 42, verse 11 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Ibn Taymiyya said in (al-Risala al-Tadmuriyya), in the first principle: Allah, glorified is He, is described by affirmation (ithbat) and negation (nafy). Affirmation is like His informing us that He is ﴿All-Knowing of everything﴾ and ﴿Able over everything﴾, that He is ﴿All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾, and similar. Negation is like His saying: ﴿Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. It should be known that negation contains no praise or perfection unless it includes an affirmation. Otherwise, mere negation contains no praise or perfection, because pure negation is pure non-existence, and pure non-existence is not a thing. What is not a thing, as it is said, is not a thing, let alone being praise or perfection. Furthermore, pure negation is predicated of the non-existent and the impossible, and the non-existent and the impossible cannot be described with praise or perfection. Therefore, most of what Allah described Himself with by way of negation includes the affirmation of a praiseworthy attribute, such as His saying: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Living, the Sustainer. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], up to His saying: ﴿and their preservation does not tire Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. The negation of drowsiness and sleep entails the perfection of life and self-subsistence, so it clarifies the perfection of His being the Living, the Sustainer. Likewise His saying: ﴿and their preservation does not tire Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], meaning it does not burden Him or weigh Him down, and this entails the perfection and completeness of His power. This is unlike the created being who is capable, when he can do something only with some strain (p. 5229) and hardship, for this is a deficiency in his power and a defect in his strength. Likewise His saying: ﴿Not an atom's weight escapes Him in the heavens or on the earth﴾ [Saba': 3]. The negation of escaping entails His knowledge of every atom in the heavens and the earth. Likewise His saying: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ [Qaf: 38]. The negation of touching by fatigue, which is weariness and exhaustion, indicates the perfection of power and the utmost of strength. This is unlike the created being, who suffers whatever weariness and fatigue befall him. Likewise His saying: ﴿Vision does not grasp Him﴾ [al-An'am: 103]. What is negated is only grasping (idrak), which is encompassing, as most scholars have said, and it does not negate mere seeing, because the non-existent is not seen, and there is no praise in His being unseen; for if that were so, the non-existent would be praiseworthy. Rather, the praise lies in His not being encompassed, even if He is seen, just as He is not encompassed even if He is known. So, just as when He is known He is not encompassed in knowledge, likewise when He is seen He is not encompassed in sight. Thus, in the negation of grasping there is an affirmation of His greatness, which is praise and an attribute of perfection. This indicates the affirmation of seeing, not its negation, but it indicates the affirmation of seeing together with the absence of encompassment. This is the truth upon which the early generations of the Ummah and its imams agreed. If you reflect on this, you will find that every negation that does not entail an established affirmation is something Allah has not described Himself with. Those who describe Him only with negative attributes (sululib) have, in reality, not affirmed a praiseworthy God, nor even an existent one. Likewise is whoever shares some of this with them, such as those who say: He does not speak, or does not see, or is not above the world, or did not settle upon the Throne. They also say: He is neither inside the world nor outside it, neither separate from the world nor adjacent to it. These attributes can be predicated of the non-existent, and they are not attributes that entail an attribute of affirmation. For this reason Mahmud ibn Subuktigin said to one who claimed this about the Creator: Distinguish for us between this Lord whom we affirm and the non-existent. Likewise, His not speaking or not descending contains no attribute of praise or perfection. Rather, these attributes contain a likening of Him to deficient or non-existent things. Some of these attributes can be predicated only of the non-existent, and some only of inanimate objects and the deficient. So whoever says: He is neither separate from the world nor in contact with the world, is like one who says: No, He is neither self-subsisting nor dependent on another, neither eternal nor originated, neither prior to the world nor coexistent with it. And whoever says: He is not living, not hearing, not seeing, not speaking, is obliged to be dead, deaf, blind, and mute. If he says: blindness is the absence of sight in what is capable of receiving sight, and what cannot receive sight, like a wall, is not called blind or seeing, it is said to him: this is a terminology you have coined. Otherwise, that which is described by lacking life, hearing, sight, and speech can be described as dead, blind, mute, and incapable of speech. Moreover, every existent is capable of being described by these matters and their opposites, for Allah is able to make inanimate matter living, just as He made Moses' staff a serpent that swallowed the ropes and staffs. Also, what cannot be described by these attributes is more deficient than what can be described by them while being described by their opposites. Thus an inanimate object, which is not described as seeing or blind, or speaking or mute, is more deficient than a living being who is blind and mute. If it is said: the Originator cannot be described by these, this is a greater ascription of deficiency to Him than if He were described as mute, blind, or deaf, and the like. Moreover, if He is made incapable of them, this is a likening of Him to an inanimate object that cannot be described by any of them. This is a likening to inanimate things, not to living beings. How then can someone who says this of Him claim that it is a likening to the Living? Furthermore, the very negation of these attributes is a deficiency, just as their affirmation is a perfection. Life, as such, apart from considering what it is attributed to, is an attribute of perfection. Likewise knowledge, power, hearing, sight, speech, intellect, and the like. Whatever is an attribute of perfection, He, glorified is He, is more worthy of being described by it than created beings. So if He were not described by it while created beings are described by it, the created being would be more perfect than Him.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:

[12, 13] ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it. Indeed, He is Knowing of all things.﴾ ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and what We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: "Establish the religion and do not be divided therein." Difficult for the polytheists is that to which you invite them. Allah chooses for it whom He wills and guides to it whoever turns back in repentance.﴾ [al-Shura: 13].

(p-5231) ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: the keys of provisions and the treasuries of dominion and the malakut (the dominion of the unseen realm). ﴿He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts﴾, meaning: He widens His provision and bounty for whom He wills of His creation and makes him rich, and He restricts it for others. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of all things﴾.

﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and what We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: "Establish the religion and do not be divided therein"﴾ [al-Shura: 13]. Know that when He, the Exalted, magnified His revelation to the Prophet ﷺ by His saying, ﴿Thus does He reveal to you, and to those before you, Allah, the Almighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Shura: 3], He mentioned in this verse the detail of that: it is what He ordained for him and for them of the agreement upon worshipping Him alone, without partner, as He said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya: 25]. And in the hadith: "We, the company of the prophets, are sons of one father (ʿallāt) and our religion is one." It means: the worship of Allah, the Exalted, alone without partner, even though their sharia (law) and their methods (manahij) differ, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a method﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48].

The singling out of these five, who are Ulu al-ʿAzm (the Possessors of Resolve, peace be upon them), by mention, is because they are the greatest of the prophets, the bearers of the great sharias and the many followers. It is also to win over the hearts of the disbelievers, since all agree on the prophethood of some of them. He began with Noah, peace be upon him, because he is the first of the messengers. The meaning: He has ordained for you of the religion (p-5232) what He enjoined upon all the prophets from the time of Noah, peace be upon him, until the time of our Prophet, upon whom be blessings and peace.

The expression of "enjoining" (tawṣiyah) regarding them and "revelation" (waḥy) regarding him is to indicate that his sharia ﷺ is the complete sharia. For this reason, he expressed it with ﴿alladhī﴾ (the one which), which is the origin of the relative pronouns. He attributed it to Himself with the pronoun of majesty, singling it out, along with his sharia, for honour, grandeur of station, and complete care. This is the secret of placing it before what follows it, despite its being earlier in time: ﴿Difficult for the polytheists is that to which you invite them﴾ [al-Shura: 13], meaning: sincere worship of Allah, affirming His divinity alone, and disavowing whatever else is worshipped besides Him of idols. ﴿Allah chooses for it whom He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 13], and this is from the turning of His choice toward what it was called to. ﴿And guides to it whoever turns back﴾ [al-Shura: 13], meaning: He grants success in acting in obedience to Him and following His messengers to whoever turns toward His obedience and repents of his disobediences.

Then, after explaining the state of the polytheists, he alluded to the People of the Book with His saying:

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[14] ﴿And they did not become divided except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term, the matter would have been decided between them. And indeed those who were given the Scripture after them are in grave doubt concerning it.﴾

﴿And they did not become divided﴾ i.e., in their religion, and they became sects (shiya'an): ﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾ i.e., the sound proofs and the certain demonstrations of the truth of what they possessed: ﴿out of rivalry among themselves﴾ i.e., out of injustice, transgression, and seeking leadership: ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term﴾ and that is the postponement of the punishment until the Day of Resurrection: ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾ i.e., by their annihilation, since their crimes deserved that: ﴿And indeed those who were given the Scripture after them﴾ and they are the people of Makkah, upon whom God bestowed the Noble Book: ﴿are in grave doubt concerning it﴾ i.e., causing their followers to fall into doubt, because of the abundance of the whisperings they spread that turn people away from the way of God.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[15] ﴿So invite (them), and be steadfast as you were commanded, and do not follow their desires. And say: "I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down. And I have been commanded to be just between you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will gather us together, and to Him is the final return."﴾

﴿So invite﴾ means: because of what has been mentioned of division and of doubt that causes unease, invite the people, all of them, to establish the religion, in order to resist falsehood and crush it, and to tear apart its whisperings. ﴿And be steadfast﴾ means: in calling to it and proclaiming it openly, ﴿as you were commanded﴾, that is, as it was revealed to you. ﴿And do not follow their desires. And say: "I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down"﴾, that is, any Book whatsoever, unlike those who believed in some and disbelieved in others. In this there is an affirmation of the truth, a statement that the Books agree in their foundations, a winning over of the hearts of the People of the Two Books, and an implicit rebuke of them. This is the view of Abu al-Su'ud.

﴿And I have been commanded to be just between you﴾ means: to treat you equally in one call, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 64]. Then He indicated that what lies beyond the aforementioned command and its delivery, of reckoning, belongs to Him, exalted is He. So He said: ﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you﴾, that is, there is no dispute and no disputation after this, because the truth has become manifest, and there is no need for argument, and no place for opposition except arrogance. The word ḥujjah (argument) is originally a verbal noun meaning the act of arguing, as al-Raghib mentioned, and it may also mean proof. What is meant here is the first, not the second, and this is evident. ﴿Allah will gather us together﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, and He will judge in truth concerning that about which we differed. ﴿And to Him is the final return﴾, that is, the return and the place of recompense.

(p-٥٢٣٤) Two reminders:

The first: interpreting justice as we have mentioned is what the context of the speech requires, especially since the surah is Meccan, and the Prophet, may Allah's blessings be upon him, did not have a role in deciding disputes and judging in rulings through it. Yes, whoever holds that this is included has only considered its generality. From this is the saying of Qatadah: "The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to be just until he died." Justice is the balance of Allah on earth, by which He takes for the oppressed from the oppressor, and for the weak from the strong, and by justice Allah confirms the truthful and refutes the liar, and by justice He repels the transgressor and rebukes him.

The second: Ibn Kathir said: this noble verse contains ten independent statements, each separate from the one before it, a judgment in its own right. They said: there is no parallel to it except the Verse of the Throne, for it too has ten such sections. End of quote.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[16] ﴿Those who dispute concerning God after He has been answered, their argument is baseless in the sight of their Lord, and upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment.﴾

﴿Those who dispute concerning God﴾ means: they argue against His religion, which He sent His seal of the prophets with. They are the ones who were given the Scripture, mentioned earlier, and they obstruct guidance, hoping for the return of *jahiliyyah* (the age of ignorance). ﴿After He has been answered﴾ means: after people have responded to Him, by submitting and yielding to His religion, as sound reason, correct reflection, the conduct and guidance of the one calling to it, the excellence of his call, the confirmation of the revealed books that came before it, and the soundness of the *fitrah* (innate human disposition) have led them to it. ﴿Their argument is baseless﴾ means: it is void, because it rests on falsehood, and falsehood cannot endure against the strength of truth. ﴿In the sight of their Lord﴾ means: in His judgment, His decree, and His determination. Abu al-Su'ud said: He described their falsehoods as an argument only by way of accommodating them, according to their false claim. ﴿And upon them is wrath﴾ means: a great wrath, because of their obstinate denial of the truth after it became manifest. ﴿And for them is a severe punishment﴾, which is the punishment of the Fire.

(p-5235) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:

[17] ﴿It is Allah who has sent down the Book with truth, and the Balance. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾

﴿It is Allah who has sent down the Book with truth﴾: i.e., accompanied by truth in its rulings and its reports. ﴿And the Balance﴾: i.e., and He sent down the Balance (al-mizan), which is justice (al-'adl), by which rights are weighed and disputes are settled. ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾: Abu al-Su'ud said: i.e., it is a near thing, or its coming is near, or "the Hour" means the Resurrection (al-ba'th). The meaning is that it is on the wing of arrival. So follow the Book, act by it, and persevere in justice before there comes upon you the Day on which deeds are weighed and their recompense is paid in full.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[18] ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth. Indeed, those who dispute about the Hour are in far-off error.﴾

﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it﴾ means: fearful of it. Ibn Jarir said: because they do not know what Allah will do to them in it. ﴿And they know that it is the truth﴾ means: whose existence is certain without doubt. ﴿Indeed, those who dispute about the Hour are in far-off error﴾ means: because of their denial of Allah's justice and His wisdom.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿Allah is Subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty.﴾ ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter.﴾ [al-Shura: 20].

(p-5236) ﴿Allah is Subtle with His servants﴾ meaning: He is gentle with them in arranging the delivery of what they need of the good of the religion and of the world. ﴿He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty.﴾ ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter.﴾ [al-Shura: 20]

Al-Zamakhshari said: What the doer does, seeking through it benefit and growth, is called "tilth" (ḥarth) in a figurative sense (majāz, meaning non-literal usage), by comparing it to sown crops, insofar as it is a benefit obtained through the work of this world. For this reason it is said: "This world is the farm of the Hereafter." There is a distinction between the deeds of the two kinds of doers: whoever works for the Hereafter is granted success in his work, and his good deeds are multiplied. Whoever's work is for this world is given some of it, not what he desires and seeks, and that is his provision which was apportioned to him and completed; and he has no share at all in the Hereafter. He did not mention, regarding the one who works for the Hereafter, that he also has a share in this world, on the basis that his apportioned provision reaches him inevitably; this is as a belittling of that in comparison with what he is aiming at, namely the growth of his deed and his success in the final return. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 42, verses 21–23:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[21–23] ﴿Or do they have partners who have instituted for them in religion that which Allah has not permitted? And were it not for the decisive word, it would have been judged between them. And indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, while it is [sure to] befall them. But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of paradise; for them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.﴾ [al-Shura: 22] ﴿That is what Allah conveys as good tidings to His servants who believed and did righteous deeds. Say, "I do not ask of you for it any payment, except affection among relatives." And whoever commits a good deed – We increase for him therein good. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾ [al-Shura: 23].

(p-5237) ﴿Or do they have partners who have instituted for them in religion that which Allah has not permitted﴾. {Am}: it is disjunctive (munqati'ah), containing the meaning of (bal, "rather," and the hamza of interrogation). There must precede it a statement, either a report or a command, which is set aside and what follows it is affirmed. What precedes His saying: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Noah﴾ [al-Shura: 13], etc., is the thing it is conjoined to, and what lies between them is a completion of the first. By "their partners" is meant either their devils, because they shared with them in disbelief and drove them to it, or their idols; and attributing them to them is because they took them as partners, even if they are not so in reality. On the second view, the attribution of legislation to them is because they are the cause of their misguidance and of their being tempted by what they practised in religion, or because they are in the form of a legislator who instituted this error for them. It is also possible that the implied interrogation is then for denial, i.e., they have neither a law nor a lawgiver, as in His saying: ﴿Or do they have gods that protect them from Us?﴾ [al-Anbiya: 43]. ﴿And were it not for the decisive word﴾, i.e., the prior decree that the recompense is on the Day of Resurrection and not in this world; or, were it not for what Allah promised them, that He will separate between them and make it clear in the Hereafter. So "separation" here means "clarification": ﴿it would have been judged between them﴾, i.e., the judgment between the disbelievers and the believers would have been completed, by hastening the punishment for the disbelievers: ﴿And indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿You will see the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Shura: 22], i.e., on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿fearful of what they have earned﴾ [al-Shura: 22], i.e., of the evil deeds: ﴿while it is [sure to] befall them﴾ [al-Shura: 22], i.e., descending upon them without doubt: ﴿But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of paradise; for them is whatever they wish with their Lord. The exception is disjunctive, and its meaning is the negation of any reward at all, because the fruit of their affection returns to them, being the cause of their salvation; so it cannot be a reward for him. It has been said: the meaning is that you should love my relatives who are your relatives, and not harm them. It has also been said: "al-qurba" means seeking nearness to Allah, i.e., except that you draw near to Allah through what brings you close to Him. The first meaning is the one the scholars relied upon, and Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, did not accept any other. In al-Bukhari, it is related from him that he was asked about His saying: ﴿except affection among relatives﴾ [al-Shura: 23], and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The relatives are the family of Muhammad." Ibn 'Abbas said: "You have been hasty. The Prophet ﷺ had no clan of Quraysh except that he had kinship with them." Then he said: "Except that you maintain the ties of kinship between me and you."

Ibn Kathir said: al-Bukhari alone narrated it (i.e., against Muslim), and Imam Ahmad narrated it. Likewise al-Sha'bi, al-Dahhak, Ali ibn Abi Talhah, al-'Awfi, Yusuf ibn Mihran, and others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, the like of it. This is also the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Abu Malik, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others.

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani, the memorizer, related: "From Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: 'I do not ask of you for it any reward except that you love me for my own sake, because of my kinship with you, and that you preserve the kinship that is between me and you.'" Imam Ahmad related from Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet ﷺ said: "I do not ask of you for what I have brought you of clear proofs and guidance any reward, except that you love Allah the Exalted, and draw near to Him by obedience to Him." Likewise it has been related from Qatadah and al-Hasan al-Basri the like of it.

As for the report that it was revealed in Medina concerning those who boasted against al-‘Abbas from the Ansar, its chain is weak. Moreover, the surah is Meccan, and no connection appears between the verse and that report in this context. Likewise what Ibn Abi Hatim related: that when this verse was revealed, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are these whose love Allah has commanded?" He said: "Fatimah and her children, may Allah be pleased with them." In its chain is an unidentified person, from a Shi'i shaykh, Husayn al-Ashqar, so his report is not accepted in this context. And mention of the revelation of the verse in Medina is far-fetched, since it is Meccan. Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with her, had no children at all at that time, for she did not marry 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, until after Badr, in the second year of the Hijrah.

The correct view is to interpret this verse by what the scholar of the Ummah and interpreter of the Qur'an, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, explained it, as al-Bukhari related from him. We do not deny the enjoining of regard for the People of the House, the command to be good to them, to honour and respect them; for they are from a pure progeny, of the most noble house that has existed upon the face of the earth, in glory, lineage, and ancestry. Especially if they follow the authentic, clear, and manifest prophetic Sunnah, as their predecessors did, such as al-'Abbas and his sons, and 'Ali and the People of his House and his descendants, may Allah be pleased with them all. It is established in the "Sahih" that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said in his sermon: "I am leaving among you the two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my family (ʿitrah). They will not separate until they come to me at the Pool." Imam Ahmad related from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, when some of Quraysh meet one another, they meet them with a good countenance, but when they meet us, they meet us with faces we do not recognize.' So the Prophet ﷺ became extremely angry and said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, faith does not enter the heart of a man until he loves you for the sake of Allah and His Messenger.'" This is the summary of what Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned, and Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah preceded him in the expansive treatment of this in "Minhaj al-Sunnah" from many aspects.

He said in the third aspect: this verse is in Surat al-Shura, and it is Meccan by the consensus of the People of the Sunnah.

Indeed, all of the Ha-Mim surahs are Meccan, and likewise the Ta-Sin surahs. It is known that 'Ali married Fatimah in Medina after the Battle of Badr; al-Hasan was born in the third year of the Hijrah, and al-Husayn in the fourth year. So this verse was revealed several years before al-Hasan and al-Husayn existed. How, then, could the Prophet ﷺ interpret the verse as the obligation of love for relatives who were not yet known and had not yet been created?

Then he said: The fourth aspect: the interpretation of the verse in the two Sahihs from Ibn 'Abbas contradicts that. Here is Ibn 'Abbas, the interpreter of the Qur'an and the most knowledgeable of the People of the House after 'Ali, saying: its meaning is not the love of the near kin; rather its meaning is: I do not ask you, O assembly of the Arabs, and O assembly of Quraysh, for any reward, but I ask you to maintain the kinship that is between me and you. So he asked the people to whom he was first sent to maintain his kin, so that they would not transgress against him until he had conveyed the message of his Lord.

The fifth aspect: he said: ﴿I do not ask of you for it any payment except affection among relatives﴾ [al-Shura: 23]; he did not say "except affection for the relatives" nor "affection for the kinsfolk." For if he had meant affection for the kinsfolk, he would have said "the affection for the kinsfolk," as He said: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger and for the near relatives﴾ [al-Anfal: 41], and He said: ﴿What Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns – it is for Allah and for the Messenger and for the near relatives﴾ [al-Hashr: 7]; likewise His saying: ﴿And give the relative his right﴾ [al-Isra: 26], and His saying: ﴿and gives wealth, in spite of love for it, to relatives﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177], and so on in many places. So all that the Qur'an mentions regarding the enjoining of rights of the relatives of the Prophet ﷺ and the relatives of a person is stated as "dhawi al-qurba" (the near kin), not "fi al-qurba." Since here He mentioned the verbal noun without the noun, this shows that He did not intend "dhawi al-qurba."

The sixth aspect: if affection for them were intended, he would have said "the affection for the kinsfolk," not "in the kinship," for one who asks for affection for another does not say: "I ask you for affection in so-and-so, or in the kinship of so-and-so." Rather he says: "I ask you for affection for so-and-so, and love for so-and-so." So when he said "affection in the kinship," it is known that the intended meaning is not "for the kinsfolk."

The seventh aspect: it may be said that the Prophet ﷺ never asked any reward for conveying the message of his Lord at all; rather his reward is with Allah, as He said: ﴿Say, "I do not ask of you any reward for it, and I am not of the pretenders"﴾ [Sad: 86], and His saying: ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ [al-Tur: 40], and His saying: ﴿Say, "Whatever reward I have asked of you is yours. My reward is only from Allah"﴾ [Saba: 47]. But the exception here is disjunctive, as He said: ﴿Say, "I do not ask of you for it any reward, except that whoever wills may take to his Lord a way"﴾ [al-Furqan: 57]. There is no doubt that love for the People of the House of the Prophet ﷺ is obligatory. But its obligation is not established by this verse, nor is their love a reward for the Prophet ﷺ; rather it is among what Allah has commanded us, as He commanded us with all the acts of worship. In the "Sahih" it is related from him that he addressed his companions at a pond called "Khumm" between Mecca and Medina, and said: "I remind you of Allah concerning my People of the House." In the "Sunan" it is related from him that he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, they will not enter Paradise until they love you for the sake of Allah and for my kinship." Whoever makes love for his People of the House a reward for himself, which he repays, has erred a grave error. And if it were a reward for him, we would not be rewarded for it, because we have given him his reward that he deserves by the message. Would a Muslim say the like of this?

The eighth aspect: "al-qurba" is definite by the article. So it must be something known to those addressed, to whom he was commanded to say: "I do not ask of you any reward for it." And it has been mentioned that when it was revealed, al-Hasan and al-Husayn had not yet been created, and 'Ali had not yet married Fatimah. Therefore the kinship which the addressees knew cannot be this one. Unlike the kinship that is between him and them, which is known to them, as you say: "I ask you only for affection in the kinship that is between us," and as you say: "I ask you only for justice between us and you," and "I ask you only that you fear Allah in this matter." End quote.

(p-5240) ﴿And whoever commits a good deed﴾ [al-Shura: 23], i.e., acquires an act of obedience: ﴿We increase for him therein good﴾ [al-Shura: 23], i.e., by multiplying it: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ [al-Shura: 23], i.e., to whoever repents and turns back: ﴿Appreciative﴾ [al-Shura: 23], of their striving, by multiplying the reward of their good deeds.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[24] ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"? So if Allah willed, He would seal over your heart. And Allah would erase falsehood and establish the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"?﴾ That is, by claiming prophethood and revelation. ﴿So if Allah willed, He would seal over your heart.﴾ Ibn Kathir said: That is, if you had fabricated a lie against Him, as these ignorant people claim, He would seal over your heart, meaning He would set a seal upon your heart and strip from you what He had given you of the Qur'an. Like His saying, majestic is His majesty: ﴿And if he had attributed to Us some sayings,﴾ [al-Haqqah: 44] ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand,﴾ [al-Haqqah: 45] ﴿then We would have cut from him the aorta,﴾ [al-Haqqah: 46] ﴿and not one of you could have prevented Us from him.﴾ [al-Haqqah: 47] That is, We would have punished him with the utmost punishment, and none of the people could have prevented Us from him. End of quotation.

This is an interpretation of the Qur'an by means of its similar verses (tafsir bil-ashbah wal-naza'ir, interpretation by parallel verses), which many of the imams prefer whenever it is possible, since the revelation explains one part of itself by another. The import of the verse on this meaning, as Abu al-Su'ud has made clear, is to argue against what they said, by showing that if he (peace be upon him) had fabricated against Allah, the Exalted, He would certainly have prevented him from that. He would have sealed his heart so that no meaning of it would occur to his mind and he would not utter a single letter of it. Since this is not the case, but rather the revelation has continued again and again, it becomes clear that it is from Allah, the Exalted.

Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿So if Allah willed, He would seal over your heart﴾ means: He would make you one of those whose hearts are sealed, so that you would fabricate a lie against Him. For no one dares to fabricate a lie against Allah except one who is in a state like theirs. This style conveys the improbability of fabrication from one like him, and that it is as far-fetched as associating partners with Allah, or entering the category of those upon whose hearts a seal has been set. Similar to this is when some trustworthy man is accused of betrayal and says, "Perhaps Allah has forsaken me; perhaps Allah has blinded my heart." He does not intend to affirm forsaking or blindness of the heart, but only to express the improbability that one like him would betray, and to draw attention to the great matter that has been brought about by accusing him of betrayal. End of quotation.

Al-Shihab said: Its meaning is: if Allah willed, He would seal over your heart as He did with them. This is a consolation for him, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, and a reminder of His kindness and honour toward him, so that he may be thankful for it and show mercy to those whose hearts were sealed and who thereby deserved their Lord's wrath. Had it not been for that, they would not have dared to attribute this to him, so it is not mentioned. This is why the particle (in) is used in place of (law), as a loosening of the reins and an allusion to the proof. Moreover, it is not conceivable that he could be described by what they mentioned. Thus the sequence (of the statement) is according to the meaning it alludes to, and its essence is that they dared to this impossibility because they are sealed upon misguidance. End of quotation.

﴿And Allah would erase falsehood and establish the truth by His words.﴾ This is a resumptive sentence (isti'naf, a new sentence) confirming the negation of fabrication from what he (ﷺ) says. For if it were fabricated, He would have obliterated it, since it is part of His practice, exalted is He, to erase falsehood and establish truth through His revelation.

So (yamhu, "erases") is not in the jussive mood by being conjoined to the conditional, but is conjoined to the whole sentence and the preceding discourse. This is why the name of Allah is repeated, and (yuhiqqu, "establishes") is in the nominative. Al-Zamakhshari said: It may also be a promise to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that He will erase the falsehood they hold, of slander and denial, and establish the truth you hold by the Qur'an and by His decree, which cannot be turned back, of your victory over them. Indeed Allah is Knowing of what is in your breast and in theirs, so the matter proceeds according to that. End of quotation.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[25] ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds, and He knows what you do.﴾

﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ means: He accepts the return of one who turns back to the Tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness) of Allah and to obedience to Him, after his disbelief. ﴿And pardons misdeeds﴾ means: the sins from which he has repented. ﴿And He knows what you do﴾ means: whether good or evil, and He will recompense you for it.

**(p-5244) The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[26, 27] ﴿And He answers those who have believed and done righteous deeds, and increases them from His bounty. As for the disbelievers, there is a severe punishment for them. And if Allah were to expand provision for His servants, they would surely rebel in the earth. But He sends down in measure what He wills. Indeed, He is Acquainted with His servants and Seeing.﴾ [ash-Shura: 27].

﴿And He answers those who have believed and done righteous deeds﴾: that is, He responds to them (yastajību lahum). The preposition *al-lām* (اللام) has been omitted, as it is omitted in His words, ﴿And when they measure for them﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 3], meaning "measure for them." That is, He rewards them for their obedience. ﴿And increases them from His bounty﴾: that is, beyond their reward, as a favor and grace from Him. ﴿As for the disbelievers, there is a severe punishment for them.﴾ ﴿And if Allah were to expand provision for His servants, they would surely rebel in the earth﴾ [ash-Shura: 27]: that is, they would transgress the limit He set for them, going beyond it to something else by committing what He has forbidden them. This is because wealth is a cause of arrogance and insolence: ﴿Nay, indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-Alaq: 6–7]. ﴿But He sends down in measure what He wills﴾ [ash-Shura: 27]: that is, but He sends down from His provision what He wills, in measure, according to what suffices them. ﴿Indeed, He is Acquainted with His servants and Seeing﴾ [ash-Shura: 27]. Al-Zamakhshari said: That is, He knows what their circumstances will lead to, so He decrees for them what is best for them and closest to uniting their affairs. Thus He makes some poor and some rich, withholds and gives, restricts and expands, as divine wisdom requires. Had He made them all rich, they would rebel; had He made them all poor, they would perish.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired, and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.﴾

﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired, and spreads His mercy﴾: that is, the blessings of the rain, its benefits, and its effects of fertility and abundance.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 42, verse 29:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[29] ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and what He has dispersed in them of living creatures. And He is, when He wills, over their gathering, All-Powerful.﴾

﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and what He has dispersed in them of living creatures, and He is over their gathering﴾, i.e., their resurrection (ḥashr) on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿when He wills, All-Powerful﴾, i.e., able to do it. Nothing is beyond Him, even if their joints are scattered.

Note:

Some researchers into the celestial verses of the Qur'an and the higher worlds have taken another meaning from this verse. Their statement reads: It is understood from the verse that God, may He be exalted, created creatures (dawabb) in the heavens, and it is inferred from His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And God created every creature from water. Of them are some that walk on their bellies, some that walk on two legs, and some that walk on four. God creates what He wills﴾ [al-Nur: 45], that these creatures are not angels as the exegetes said, but animals like the animals of the earth, and it is not far-fetched that among them there is a rational animal like man. The life of those animals necessitates that there be in the heavens plants, trees, seas and rivers, as has been established in this age among the scientists of observation.

Then he said: By my life, this verse which was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ) one thousand three hundred and twenty years ago is indeed a sign for the people of this age, and what a sign it is: a sign for the people of knowledge and philosophy who spend wealth and lives without limit or reckoning, in order to reach knowledge of a secret of the secrets of existence. And despite this intense effort and continuous exertion for three hundred years, they have reached, only by conjecture, nothing of what this verse has informed of.

(p-5246) The most that they have reached by rational proof is that the earth is smaller than the sun, that it revolves around it, that the wandering planets are spheres, and that the fixed stars are suns, having wandering bodies revolving around them. When they all established the existence of water and air, and the occurrence of summer and winter on these planets, they supposed that there exists in them a world like the world of the earth.

Some of them began to think of devising means of communication by electricity with the inhabitants of Mars, which is the nearest of the planets to us, and that is not impossible in terms of technique. Its possibility is inferred from the end of this same verse, His words, may He be exalted: ﴿and He is over their gathering, when He wills, All-Powerful﴾. So it is not far-fetched that they might communicate and unite in thought, if they cannot unite in body. Let the astronomers look at what this verse contains, the treasure hidden in the Qur'an. And let those of us who are impressed by modern sciences, who turn away from Islamic sciences, know what wisdom and clarity is in the Book of God. He also said: It is not hidden that the Great Qur'an was revealed primarily and essentially to explain the truth and teach the religion. But, as a preparation for this path, it brought fragments of astronomical and natural sciences, and turned the insights of people to reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth and what they possess of innovation, and directed their gaze to contemplate the creation of man and what he has of wondrous composition, along with other astronomical and natural matters, in more than three hundred verses.

So the exegetes, may God have mercy on them, when they explained these verses, explained their meanings according to the extent of their knowledge of astronomical and natural sciences, and it is not hidden how deficient these instruments were in their time, especially astronomy. They are excused if they did not grasp the meanings of these verses, which bewilder the minds of the philosophers of this age, who are versed in rational sciences. Therefore they did not explain these verses with their true explanation, but rather interpreted them and turned their meanings away from the literal to the figurative or metaphorical. End of his words.

Another astronomer also said: The scholars say: it is established that these planets are inhabited by creatures resembling the creatures on this our earth, and each planet is an earth with respect to its creatures, and the rest of the planets are heavens with respect to it.

(p-5247) He said: The apparent view is that the claim of the existence of creatures on these planets is correct, because God, may He be exalted, says in His Book: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and what He has dispersed in them of living creatures, and He is over their gathering, when He wills, All-Powerful﴾, and He says: ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him; every day He is in a matter﴾ [al-Rahman: 29].

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:

[30] ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned; and He pardons much.﴾

﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned⦆ That is: it is because of your acts of disobedience, and the sins you have committed. ﴿And He pardons much⦆ That is: of the sins, so He does not punish for them.

The discussion of His words, exalted is He:

[31] ﴿And you cannot escape [Allah] within the earth, and you have no protector or helper other than Allah.﴾

﴿And you cannot escape within the earth﴾ — i.e., you cannot escape your Lord if He wills to punish you, because you are in the grip of His control. ﴿And you have no protector or helper other than Allah﴾ — i.e., if He wills to chastise you. So fear Him and be in awe of Him.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[32–33] ﴿And among His signs are the ships, running in the sea like mountains﴾ ﴿If He wills, He stills the wind, and they remain motionless on its surface. Surely in that are signs for everyone who is steadfast and grateful﴾ [al-Shura: 33].

﴿And among His signs are the ships (al-jawari)﴾, that is, the sailing vessels, ﴿running in the sea like mountains (al-a'lam)﴾, that is, like mountains.

(p-5248) ﴿If He wills, He stills the wind, and they remain motionless on its surface﴾ [al-Shura: 33], that is, they will remain fixed on the surface of the sea. ﴿Surely in that﴾ [al-Shura: 33], that is, in the running of these ships upon the sea by God Exalted's subjecting of the wind to their motion, ﴿are signs﴾ [al-Shura: 33], that is, a lesson, an admonition, and a clear proof of the eternal power, ﴿for everyone who is steadfast and grateful﴾ [al-Shura: 33], that is, for every believer. He specifically chose these two mentioned attributes as a reminder of what the believer should possess of abundant patience and much gratitude, since faith is not complete without them both. (Faith is two halves: one half is patience, and one half is gratitude.)

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 42, verse 39:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿And those who, when wrongful oppression afflicts them, they defend themselves.﴾

﴿And those who, when wrongful oppression afflicts them, they defend themselves﴾ i.e., with justice, avoiding humiliation and being wronged, because they are in a station of uprightness, standing firm for the truth and justice whose shadow is in their souls. Said al-Qashani.

Ibn Jarir said: The interpreters differed concerning the oppressor whom God, may His remembrance be exalted, praised the one who defends himself against after his oppression of him. Some of them said: it is the polytheist when he oppresses the Muslim. Others said: rather, it is every oppressor who oppresses, so He praised the one who defends himself against him. This is the view of al-Suddi, where he said: "They defend themselves against those who oppress them, without transgressing."

Ibn Jarir said: This second view is more correct in its validity, because God did not specify one meaning over another. Rather, the praise is for every one who defends himself rightfully against the one who oppressed him. If someone says: What is there in self-defence of praise? It is said: Indeed, in establishing the wrongdoer upon the path of truth and punishing him with what he deserves, there is a correction of him, and in that is the greatest praise. End.

Al-Zamakhshari said likewise. If you say: Are they praiseworthy in self-defence? I say: Yes, because whoever takes his right, not transgressing God's limit and what He commanded, does not exceed in killing if he is a guardian of blood, or responds to a foolish person in defence of his honour and as a deterrent to him, then he is obedient, and every obedient person is praiseworthy. Al-Nakha'i said: They used to dislike humbling themselves, lest the wicked become emboldened against them.

Then He, exalted is He, indicated that self-defence must be restricted to an equal measure, by His saying:

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[40–42] ﴿The recompense for an evil is an evil like it, but whoever pardons and makes amends, his reward is with Allah. Indeed, He does not love wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿And whoever avenges himself after being wronged, those—there is no path against them.﴾ [al-Shura: 41] ﴿The path is only against those who wrong people and transgress upon the earth without right. For them is a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Shura: 42]

﴿The recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾: that is, the recompense for the evil deed of the one who does wrong is what is equal to it, since taking less is unjust (*hayf*) and taking more is oppression (*zulm*). Then He, exalted is He, made clear that pardon is better, so He said: ﴿but whoever pardons and makes amends﴾: that is, between himself and his adversary, by pardoning and overlooking. ﴿his reward is with Allah﴾: that is, his reward is upon Him. In leaving its (the reward's) amount unspecified there is an indication of its greatness, since it has been made an obligation upon the Mighty, the Generous. ﴿Indeed, He does not love wrongdoers﴾: that is, those who initiate the evil deed and those who exceed the limits in retaliation. ﴿And whoever avenges himself after being wronged﴾ [al-Shura: 41]: that is, after he has been wronged. The verbal noun (*masdar*) here is in construct with its object, or it is the verbal noun of the passive form (*mabni lil-maf'ul*). ﴿There is no path against them﴾ [al-Shura: 41]: that is, against the one who punishes in kind, nor against the one who blames or reproaches, because they have taken their right from them justly. Whoever takes his right from one upon whom that is obligatory, without transgressing and without wronging, how could there be a path against him?

﴿The path is only against those who wrong people﴾ [al-Shura: 42]: that is, who initiate wrong and harm, (p-5251) or who exceed the limits in retaliation. ﴿and transgress upon the earth without right﴾ [al-Shura: 42]: that is, who act arrogantly therein and cause corruption. ﴿For them is a painful punishment﴾ [al-Shura: 42]: that is, because of their wrongdoing and their transgression.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[43] ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾

﴿And whoever is patient﴾, i.e., over the harm. ﴿and forgives﴾, i.e., the one who wronged him, and does not take retribution. ﴿Indeed that is of the matters requiring determination﴾, i.e., those which God urged His servants toward, and resolved that they act upon.

A note (tanbih):

Al-Suyuti (d. 911 AH) reported in "al-Iklil" from al-Kiya al-Harrasi (al-Kiya al-Harrasi), that he said: "God has urged forgiveness in several places in His Book. The apparent meaning of this verse, ﴿And those who, when tyranny strikes them, they defend themselves﴾ [al-Shura: 39], is that retaliation (intisar) is more excellent." He said: "This is to be understood as applying to one who transgresses and persists, lest the wicked become emboldened against the people of religion; and the verses of pardon refer to one who regrets and desists." End of quotation.

It is strange that he derives the superiority from the verse, for it does not indicate it, neither by expression nor by allusion. God, exalted is He, did not encourage retaliation; rather He made clear that it is permitted for them if they wish. Then He clarified after it that its permissibility is conditional upon observing equivalence, then He showed that pardon is better, and this is where the discourse reaches its conclusion and the context is complete. Likewise there is no need to restrict retaliation to the one who transgressed. That is because retaliation in kind is among the branches of the science of penalties and recompense, which are prescribed to establish truth and justice, to repel injustice from the self, to avoid humiliation, and to remove resentments and grudges. As for pardon and overlooking, these belong to the branches of the science of ethics and the refinement of souls, because it is a matter of showing leniency regarding one's right and forgoing what one is entitled to, out of desire for purifying the self, subduing it, and eagerness for the better of the two outcomes and the greater of the two rewards. Both are among the virtues of the upright (al-Hanifiyyah) Sharia, and of its moderation between strict retribution (al-iqtisas al-batta) and total pardon (al-afw kulliyyan), because sound reason sees in each of them excess and deficiency. The religion is the religion of natural disposition (al-fitrah), and natural disposition demands retaliation in kind and regards it as a right by its very constitution. The moral judgment (al-qada' al-adabi) and the divine inner restraint (al-wazi' al-rahmani) guide it toward what is more excellent, if it wills, and demonstrate to it the excellence of that course, (p-5252) so it is not far, if it reflects upon itself and returns to its right guidance, that it prefers that and does not prefer anything over it. How could it be otherwise, when His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Shura: 40], indicates, as al-Zamakhshari said, that retaliation can hardly be secured against exceeding the bounds of the offense and transgression, especially in a state of anger and the blaze of zeal. Thus the one who retaliates may be among the wrongdoers while not being aware of it.

﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no protector after Him﴾ That is: whomever Allah forsakes from right guidance, there is no protector for him who could take charge of him, guide him to the path of rectitude, and keep him firm after Allah has sent him astray. ﴿And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying, "Is there any way to return?"﴾ That is: a return to the world. The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[48] ﴿But if they turn away, We have not sent you as a watcher over them. Your duty is only to convey (the message). Indeed, when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it; but if an evil befalls them because of what their hands have put forward, then indeed man is ungrateful.﴾

﴿But if they turn away, We have not sent you as a watcher over them﴾: i.e., a guardian, watching over their deeds and keeping account of them. ﴿Your duty is only to convey (the message)﴾: i.e., conveying to them what you were sent with. If you have done so, then you have discharged what is incumbent upon you. ﴿Indeed, when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it; but if an evil befalls them because of what their hands have put forward, then indeed man is ungrateful﴾: i.e., denier of the blessings of his Lord. (p-5254)

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying:

[49–50] ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills. Or He pairs them off, males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren. Indeed He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.﴾ [al-Shura: 50]

That is: He, exalted is He, makes the circumstances of the servants regarding children differ according to what His will requires. The mention of females first is either because they are more numerous, for the increase of offspring, or to console their fathers' hearts, alerting that they are a cause of the increase of His creatures. Therefore it is not permissible to grieve over their birth or to dislike them, as is observed in some ignorant people. Al-Tha'alibi said: it is an indication of the blessing (yumn) in the early birth of females, and "among the blessings of a woman is that her first child is a girl."

Al-Shihab said: the pronoun in ﴿they﴾ [al-Shura: 50] refers to the children, and what follows it is a circumstantial clause (hal) from it, or a second object if the verb is taken to imply "making" (al-tasyir). That is, He makes the children of whomever He wills both males and females paired; just as He makes some of them exclusively males and some exclusively females, and makes some of them have no children at all.
