The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[51] ﴿It is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger who reveals, by His permission, whatever He wills. Indeed He is Most High, Wise.﴾

﴿It is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation﴾ i.e., by inspiration and a casting into the heart from Him, without an intermediary. ﴿Or from behind a veil﴾ i.e., He speaks to him in such a way that he hears His speech without seeing Him, as He spoke to Musa, peace be upon him. ﴿Or by sending a messenger﴾ i.e., from among the angels, such as Jibril. ﴿Who reveals, by His permission, whatever He wills﴾ i.e., that messenger reveals to the one to whom he is sent, by the permission of his Lord, whatever He wills to reveal of command, prohibition and other matters, by way of casting, breathing into the heart, inspiration, or a voice, or a dream. ﴿Indeed He is Most High﴾ i.e., too exalted to be confronted and addressed. Rather, whoever confronts Him perishes and vanishes, because of His loftiness, such that nothing else can remain with Him or bear His presence. Thus said al-Qashani.

Al-Mahayimi said: i.e., a human cannot attain the limit of speaking with Him face to face, nor can the hearing of His speech be borne together with seeing Him. End of quotation.

﴿Wise﴾ i.e., He arranges with wisdom the modes of speaking, so that His knowledge may appear in the detailed manifestations, and His servants may be perfected by it and be guided to Him so that they may know Him. Al-Mahayimi said: i.e., Wise in conveying His exalted speech to frail humanity.

Note (tanbih):

In al-Iklil, ʿĀ'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, used this verse as evidence that the Prophet ﷺ did not see his Lord. Malik used His saying ﴿or by sending a messenger﴾ as evidence that whoever swears not to speak to Zayd, and then sends a messenger or a letter to him, breaks his oath, because He excepted it from speech, which indicates that it is included in speech. End of quotation. But this is far-fetched, since one does not say of someone whom Allah has inspired that He spoke to him except metaphorically, so the exception would not be a connected (istithna' muttasil) one.

And His exalted saying:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[52, 53] ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor [what] faith [was], but We made it a light, by which We guide whomever We will of Our servants. And indeed, you guide to a straight path, the path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Unquestionably, to Allah are the matters returned.﴾ [al-Shura: 52–53]

﴿And thus﴾ i.e., like that revelation, through the three means: ﴿We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command﴾ i.e., revelation from Our command. He named it "spirit" because dead hearts are given life by it. Al-Shihab said: it is a metaphor (isti'ara) or an unrestricted metonymy (majaz mursal), because of the guidance and knowledge in it, which is like life. It was also said: it is Jibril.

(p-5256) {We have revealed} is implicitly (mudammin) the meaning of "We sent." The meaning: We sent it to you with the revelation: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it﴾ i.e., the spirit, or the Book, or faith, ﴿a light by which We guide whomever We will of Our servants﴾ i.e., by granting success in accepting it and reflecting upon it. ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path, the path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [al-Shura: 53] i.e., in creation and dominion. ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah are the matters returned﴾ [al-Shura: 53] i.e., in the Hereafter, when He will judge between them with justice, since there is no judge other than Him, and He will recompense each according to what he deserves of reward or punishment. We ask Almighty Allah to make our return good. Indeed, He is the Generous, the Giver.
